summary: United Campus Workers of Arizona was founded on September 1, 2020, when workers in coalitions formed that year at the University of Arizona and ASU voted to affiliate with the Communications Workers of America. Workers at ASU began organizing with the union in December 2021.
Contract talks between BU and BUGWU began in July 2023.
Some BUGWU members went on strike in March 2024; the seven-month strike, the longest in BU's history, ended with ratification in October 2024.
BUGWU members ratified their first contract on October 16, 2024, 87% in favor and 13% against.

The National Labor Relations Board certified BUGWU as the bargaining representative in Case No. 01-RC-305360 on December 16, 2022; the University's recognition of the union rests on that certification.
note: The agreement gives no date for the certification; the date is from the board's case docket, which names the certified union as Service Employees International Union, Local 509.

summary: In a National Labor Relations Board election, Boston University's graduate student employees voted 1,414 to 28 for representation by SEIU Local 509, the union BUGWU joined.
note: The board's tally lists 3,206 eligible voters, 1,442 ballots counted and 313 challenged ballots, which did not affect the result.

summary: Brown recognizes GLO as the exclusive bargaining representative of its Graduate Student Employees, as certified by the American Arbitration Association on December 6, 2018.
Bargaining for GLO's next contract began in February 2023; the union announced a first session between its bargaining committee and Brown's administration for Wednesday, February 15, 2023.

The previous (2020) agreement was due to expire on June 30, 2023; on June 28, Brown said the sides remained far apart and no successor or extension was expected by then, although bargaining had been under way since February.
In mid-November 2023 GLO and Brown reached agreement on stipends and on discrimination and harassment clauses, a breakthrough in talks that began in February.
note: The Herald article is dated Wednesday, November 22, 2023, so "last Wednesday" is November 15.

summary: GLO members voted electronically on whether to ratify the tentative agreement; voting opened December 11 and ran through midnight on Monday, December 18, 2023.
note: The post does not report the result.

summary: Bargaining for a successor contract began in February 2026. GLO opened with a 12% base stipend increase for FY27 (a $58,462 stipend), then 11% in FY28 and 10% in FY29; Brown countered with a 6.7% stipend increase over five years, which the union describes as a 0% raise in the first year.
Graduate fellows sought union recognition in March 2026 under a new Rhode Island law covering all graduate students; Brown declined to recognize them voluntarily on April 13, 2026.
The 2023 agreement expired at 11:59 pm on June 30, 2026, with bargaining for its successor still under way.

GLO grew out of Stand Up for Graduate Students (SUGS), formed in 2014 in response to a crisis in sixth-year funding for PhD students; in 2016 SUGS became Stand Up For Graduate Student Employees (SUGSE) and began organizing towards a labor union of graduate workers.

On December 16, 2017 the National Labor Relations Board dismissed Columbia's objections to the December 2016 election and certified Graduate Workers of Columbia-UAW. The agreement recognizes the union as exclusive bargaining representative for wages, hours and working conditions of employees in the unit certified in Case No. 02-RC-143012.
note: The agreement gives no certification date; the date is the union's account, and the Board's case docket lists a Board decision on that day. The union's history says Columbia still refused to bargain after the certification, which led to a strike in April 2018.

summary: The graduate-student workers first walked off their research, teaching and administrative jobs on March 15.
note: The article gives no year and no end date for this walkout.

summary: A 10-week strike by graduate instructors and others ended on January 7, 2022, the day after the two sides reached a tentative agreement.
note: The start date is not given in the sources.

summary: Union members voted 97 percent in favor of ratifying the contract, according to a January 28 email from the provost.
Graduate student workers at Columbia began organizing a union in January 2014, and in the fall of 2014 Graduate Workers of Columbia (GWC-UAW) collected union cards from more than 1,700 of them.
In a National Labor Relations Board election held December 7 and 8, 2016 and counted December 9, the union won 1,602 votes to 623.
note: The vote followed the Board's August 23, 2016 Columbia University decision, which restored the right of graduate research and teaching assistants at private universities to bargain collectively. Columbia objected to the election, delaying certification until December 2017.

summary: The University announced that CGSU-UE members and the University had ratified the first collective bargaining agreement.
Graduate workers voted 1,873 to 80 to form a union with the United Electrical, Radio and Machine Workers of America in a National Labor Relations Board election held November 6 to 9, 2023.
note: The union began collecting membership cards on September 6, 2023. An earlier campaign, affiliated with the American Federation of Teachers, lost its March 2017 election; an arbitrator later found that a Graduate School dean's email before that vote violated federal labor law.

summary: The National Labor Relations Board certified the election result on November 20, 2023, the union reports.
The Professional Staff Congress was created on April 14, 1972, by the merger of the Legislative Conference and the United Federation of College Teachers.
PSC-CUNY members ratified the 2023-2027 agreement, 90% of those voting in favor, with 66% of eligible members voting over three weeks; the chancellor announced the result on January 14, 2025.
PhD students voted to unionize in an NLRB election, 1,000 to 131 (88% voting yes).
note: The date is that of the vote count reported by The Chronicle the same day.

summary: After almost two years of bargaining, the union's bargaining committee reached a full tentative agreement with the Duke administration.
Union members ratified the first contract, with 99% of those voting in favor.
note: The page is the union's Ratification 2025 page; only union members could vote.

summary: Duke graduate students formed the Duke Graduate Students Union as a direct-action, direct-join union in spring 2017, after an inconclusive NLRB election; organizing with SEIU had begun in early 2016.
The NLRB certified the results of the August 2023 election, making the union the PhD students' exclusive bargaining representative; Duke recognizes it under that certification.
note: The union's history page dates the certification only as a week after the vote count of August 22, 2023.

summary: Graduate students, staff and faculty began organizing a chapter of United Campus Workers of Georgia at Georgia Tech in fall 2018.

United Campus Workers of Virginia announced its George Mason University chapter at a May Day rally on the Fairfax campus, after two years of organizing by campus workers, graduate students among them.
A three-day strike in 2021 preceded the ratification of the 2021 agreement.
note: The source gives the year only.

summary: The 2021 agreement was ratified in 2021, following a three-day strike.
note: The source gives the year only. Harvard's bargaining page refers to the ratification of both a 2020 and a 2021 contract with HGSU-UAW.

summary: Bargaining for a successor to the 2021 agreement began in March 2025; by October 9, 2026 the parties had held 36 formal and six informal sessions without reaching a contract (Harvard's account).
HGSU-UAW members approved a strike authorization vote in late March 2026.
Strike from April 21 to June 1, 2026, which the union ended without a collective bargaining agreement.

Harvard's August 18, 2026 compensation proposal (not agreed): a single RA minimum for all disciplines, raised 6.07% on ratification to $51,972, then 2.5% on July 1, 2027 and 2028 and 2.75% on July 1, 2029 ($56,100 in FY30), with PhD Teaching Fellows raised to parity with RAs; hourly minimum $22.50 on ratification rising to $24.00 by July 1, 2029. Superseded by the University's October 2026 proposal.
note: A proposal only, so no rates are recorded for it. The date is from the proposal's title on Harvard's bargaining page, which described this proposal until October 2026.

summary: Harvard's October 2026 compensation proposal (not agreed), dated October 8, 2026: as in August, a single RA minimum for all disciplines raised 6.07% on ratification to $51,972, but then 3% on each of July 1, 2027, 2028 and 2029 ($56,796 in FY30), with PhD Teaching Fellows raised to parity with RAs; the hourly minimum is unchanged from August, $22.50 on ratification rising to $24.00 by July 1, 2029.
note: A proposal only, so no rates are recorded for it. The bargaining page rounds the ratification increase to 6.1%.

summary: HGSU-UAW members approved a second strike authorization vote in October 2026.

The graduate student unionization effort at Harvard became public in April 2015; organizers trace its roots to the Occupy Harvard movement of 2011. Later in 2015 the union voted to affiliate with the United Automobile Workers.

Harvard's first unionization election, in November 2016, did not produce a union majority: the revised tally was 1,396 for and 1,526 against. The National Labor Relations Board found the university's voter lists deficient and ordered a second election.
In the second election, held April 18 and 19, 2018, eligible student workers voted 1,931 to 1,523 to be represented by HGSU-UAW.
The National Labor Relations Board certified HGSU-UAW as the representative of Harvard's student workers on April 30, 2018, after neither side objected to the election.
Teachers and Researchers United began as a small group of graduate workers in 2014; it has organized with the United Electrical, Radio and Machine Workers of America (UE) since 2021.
About 3,200 PhD student workers voted in a union election and chose TRU-UE to represent them in collective bargaining with the university.
note: The dates come from the headline summaries of two JHU Hub stories listed beside the ratification article, published January 23, 2023 (announcing the election on January 30 and 31) and February 1, 2023 (reporting the result). The vote tally is not given.

summary: Union-represented PhD students voted to ratify the three-year agreement, whose terms had been reached on March 29, 2024, after more than 40 bargaining sessions that began in May 2023.
In a National Labor Relations Board election on April 4 and 5, 2022, MIT graduate workers voted 1,785 to 912 to be represented by UE.
MIT recognizes the Union as the sole and exclusive bargaining agent for graduate students employed to provide instructional or research services (RAs, TAs and instructor Gs).
note: The agreement gives no recognition date.

summary: The union kicked off negotiations for its first MIT contract with a rally on September 12, 2022.

Strike threat, not a strike: the union's account is that after it publicly announced a strike plan, and 24 hours before it was due to launch a public strike pledge, it won a tentative agreement on its first contract.
The union reports ratifying its first contract by Friday, September 22, 2023, ending a 12-month negotiation with MIT.
MIT and the union began bargaining a successor contract on April 24, 2026; five sessions had been held by June 4, 2026.

In late May 2026 MIT offered a 12-month contract extension with an immediate 3% raise for all union members; on June 1 the union declined it at the bargaining table without putting it to members (MIT's account) and proposed a 3-month extension, which MIT rejected.
note: The letter is dated Thursday, June 4, 2026, so the Monday on which the union declined the offer was June 1.

summary: MIT's letter reports that the 2023 agreement expired on May 31, 2026 and that most of its terms remain in effect until a new contract is signed.

On October 7, 2026 MIT and the union held a thirteenth negotiating session toward a new contract; the union presented a comprehensive proposal package and tentative agreements were reached on grievance procedure, nondiscrimination, workload and childcare. No successor agreement existed.

MIT graduate workers began meeting to discuss organizing a union in 2018; by late 2019 the organizing committee was looking at affiliating with a national union, and it announced its union drive publicly in September 2021.

Graduate students at NJIT formed the union in 2010 as the Union of Contingent Academics at NJIT, a local of the American Federation of Teachers; postdocs joined in 2012, when the first contract was won.
New Jersey's Public Employment Relations Commission announced on July 13, 2010, that NJIT's graduate and postdoctoral workers had voted to unionize, certifying the union.
UCAN members ratified the GSRE and adjunct agreements in a vote ending January 30, 2024, with more than 99 percent of those voting in favor.
note: Dated from the union's account, which says the vote ended Tuesday, January 30. NJIT's Human Resources page says the agreement was ratified on January 31, 2024, and Patch, reporting February 1, dates the vote to Wednesday (January 31); the union may have announced the result the day after the vote closed.

summary: The 2022-2026 agreement expired June 30, 2026, without a successor.

As of October 2026, UCAN and NJIT were bargaining successor contracts for July 1, 2026 - June 30, 2030, about to take up pay, health insurance, and other economic issues; the next GSRE session was set for October 21, 2026.
Northwestern University Graduate Workers formed in 2016, after the National Labor Relations Board's Columbia decision affirmed graduate workers' right to unionize.
In a National Labor Relations Board election in January 2023, over 93% of graduate workers who voted chose NUGW-UE.
note: The union's timeline gives the month but not the day of the vote.

summary: The University recognizes NUGW-UE as exclusive bargaining agent under the NLRB's Certification of Representation in Case No. 13-RC-307313.
note: The agreement gives no certification date.

summary: Graduate workers ratified their first collective bargaining agreement in March 2024, after months of negotiations; the University dates ratification to March 15, 2024.
GSOC first won recognition in 2001, the first graduate union at a US private university.
A three-week strike, beginning Monday, April 26, 2021, after nearly a year of bargaining, preceded the 2020-2026 agreement.
note: Washington Square News reported on April 29, 2021 that the strike entered its third day on Wednesday, April 28, with picketing every day since Monday, which dates its start to April 26. No cited source gives the date it ended.

summary: Members ratified the agreement with a 99% yes vote on June 6, 2021.
GSOC moved from UAW Local 2110 to UAW Local 7902, which also represents NYU's contract faculty, after a membership-wide vote.
The agreement ran through August 31, 2026; either party could request successor negotiations from April 1, 2026.

Bargaining for a successor agreement was under way by the end of May 2026 (the June 1 update reports the second session). The October 7, 2026 update, after the 11th session, reports a tentative agreement on the Posting article and continuing talks on other articles.
note: None of the updates reports a full tentative agreement or any agreed pay figures.

summary: The Graduate Student Organizing Committee was established in 1998.
note: From the scope note of NYU Libraries' Tamiment Library finding aid for the union's archived website, which also dates its first contract with NYU to 2002.

summary: Graduate employees voted 620 to 10 for GSOC-UAW and SET-UAW as their union in a December 2013 election certified by the American Arbitration Association, after NYU had stopped recognizing the union following the National Labor Relations Board's 2004 Brown University decision.
note: The union announced the result on December 12, 2013. Under its agreement with NYU, the university then recognized the union and began bargaining a new contract.

summary: After the December 2013 election, NYU recognized GSOC-UAW again under its agreement with the union, and bargaining for a new contract began.
Graduate workers formed the Coalition of Graduate Employees in 2014 after a sudden, unannounced increase in their health insurance premiums. CGE voted to affiliate with the UAW in summer 2022.
note: The union's timeline also records a first union election in 2017-2018 that failed by a margin of 3 to 2.

summary: CGE-UAW petitioned the PLRB on December 4, 2024; on-site voting ran October 21 (Hershey) and October 27-29, 2025 (University Park), plus mail ballots, and the November 13, 2025 count gave 1,882 votes for CGE-UAW and 198 for no representative, of 2,241 ballots cast; 156 ballots were challenged and 5 were void.
note: The union's website reports 98 "no" votes; the Board's count is 198.

summary: Preliminary certification: the PLRB issued a nisi (preliminary) order certifying CGE-UAW as exclusive representative of graduate assistants serving as teaching, research, or administrative support assistants, to become final absent exceptions within 20 days.
Penn State filed exceptions with the PLRB challenging only the inclusion of research assistants in the unit; it said it would begin negotiating for teaching and administrative support assistants.
note: No PLRB decision or contract appears in the sources as of October 2026.

summary: The University recognizes the union as the exclusive bargaining representative of Graduate Workers under the NLRB certification in Case No. 04-RC-327396, which followed the 2024 election.
GETUP-UAW Local 5124 members ratified the first contract.
The University and GETUP-UAW reached a tentative agreement setting a $49,000 minimum annual stipend and a $25 minimum hourly rate.

The current union has its roots in the summer of 2020, according to one of its organizers. It took the name of earlier campaigns at Penn: a first GET-UP, affiliated with the American Federation of Teachers, formed in April 2001, and an effort revived in 2017 withdrew its election petition in February 2018.
note: The Daily Pennsylvanian describes today's union, in its organizer's words, as a separate organization that uses the name of the earlier efforts.

summary: Graduate workers voted 1,807 to 97 for representation by the UAW in a National Labor Relations Board election whose tally was issued on May 3, 2024.

Graduate students rejected unionization with Princeton Graduate Students United (PGSU), which intended to affiliate with UE, 652 to 391 (63% against), in an NLRB election held May 13 and 14, 2024. About half of graduate students were eligible: those titled "assistant in instruction" or "assistant in research", primarily in the natural sciences and engineering.

Graduate students began organizing Princeton Graduate Students United (PGSU) in 2016, after the National Labor Relations Board's ruling that year that graduate students at private universities may unionize. The drive paused after 2017, resumed with an affiliation with the United Electrical, Radio and Machine Workers of America (UE) announced in February 2023, and lost its election in May 2024.

Rutgers full-time faculty unionized in 1970 with the Rutgers chapter of the American Association of University Professors, a professional association chapter since its first meeting on November 2, 1922.
Teaching assistants and graduate assistants were added to the full-time faculty bargaining unit in 1972.

Bargaining for a successor to the 2022-2026 agreement (proposed by the union as a 2026-2030 agreement) began with the union's opening proposals on March 25, 2026 and was still under way at the October 8, 2026 session. The union's FAQ on graduate funding, written during bargaining, said its TA/GA article proposal had not reached tentative agreement.

Stanford graduate workers formed the Stanford Graduate Workers Union with the United Electrical, Radio and Machine Workers of America (UE) in spring 2023, signing 2,571 union cards on the first day of the campaign; the union election passed nine weeks after the campaign began.
note: UE's account says some alumni had been involved in the initial stages of organizing about three years earlier. The union filed its petition for an election with the National Labor Relations Board on April 27, 2023.

summary: In the National Labor Relations Board election, 1,639 voted for representation by UE (Graduate Students United) and 108 against, of 3,410 eligible voters; the NLRB issued the tally on July 6, 2023.
note: The NLRB issued the notice of election on May 18, 2023; the date recorded is the tally's.

summary: The NLRB certified UE as the exclusive representative of Stanford's graduate workers on July 14, 2023; the 2024 agreement's recognition article rests on that certification.
SGWU members ratified their first contract with Stanford.
The New York Public Employment Relations Board certified GSEU as the representative of the State University Graduate Student Negotiating Unit on December 30, 1992 (Case C-2894).

Graduate Students United formed in the spring of 2007 as an independent union of graduate student workers; it affiliated with the United Electrical, Radio and Machine Workers of America (UE) on August 25, 2022.
Graduate students were scheduled to vote on unionizing with GSU-UE in an election on January 31 and February 1, 2023.
note: The Chicago Maroon article, published January 22, 2023, gives the scheduled dates before the vote; it does not report the result. The NLRB certified the unit on March 24, 2023.

summary: The NLRB certified the graduate student employee bargaining unit in Case No. 13-RC-307974; the agreement's recognition clause also cites a second certification, Case No. 13-RC-335852.
The Graduate Employee Organization was formally recognized as a union in 1990, after graduate students at UMass Amherst had organized for a union since the 1970s.
A ten-day strike in 1991 brought the administration back to the bargaining table, and GEO won its first contract that year.
Graduate workers organizing at UMD voted in the summer of 2023 to seek affiliation with the United Auto Workers (UAW).
The Graduate Labor Union, formerly known as Fearless Student Employees, launched its public campaign for unionization as a UAW campaign, asking a majority of graduate workers to sign union cards.
note: The Diamondback's article of September 7, 2023 dates the launch rally to the preceding Monday. The union's pages and the article don't say when the earlier group was formed.

summary: The Governor approved HB 141 (Chapter 774), which gives graduate assistants at the University of Maryland, College Park collective bargaining rights from July 1, 2028.
Negotiations on a successor to the 2023-2026 agreement began November 14, 2025, with a mediator from the Michigan Employment Relations Commission that the university had requested.

Graduate Student Research Assistants voted to join the GEO bargaining unit in an election run by the Michigan Employment Relations Commission, 299 to 25 (six spoiled ballots), with 17% of the 1,910 eligible voters casting ballots.
The 2023-2026 agreement reached its May 1, 2026 end date without a successor; under Article XXVI it continues in force unless either party gives 30 days' notice of termination.

Citing slow progress, the university asked the Michigan Employment Relations Commission to begin fact-finding; by September 18, 2026 the university had offered 2.5% a year over four years and GEO 9% a year (or CPI, if higher) over three years.
At the twenty-fourth negotiation session, GEO rejected the comprehensive package the university had proposed on September 18, 2026, and continued to present individual proposals.
GEO dates its founding to 1970, when teaching fellows first organized, as the University Teaching Fellows' Union, and petitioned the Michigan Employment Relations Commission for an election.
note: GEO's history page says the 1970 petition was denied in 1971, and that the name Graduate Employees Organization came in a second drive, when the Organization of Teaching Fellows (formed in 1973) joined research and staff assistants before the 1974 certification election.

summary: The Michigan Employment Relations Commission certified GEO as bargaining agent on April 15, 1974, after a certification election GEO won 807 to 424.

UAW 4811 dates its formation to 1999, when academic student employees at UC voted for UAW representation; the graduate local was then UAW 2865, which later merged with the postdocs' UAW 5810 to become UAW 4811.

Teaching assistants, readers and tutors voted for UAW representation in campus elections run by the Public Employment Relations Board (PERB) in spring 1999: UCLA in March, Berkeley on May 13 (833 for, 293 against), and the remaining six campuses by June.
note: The Berkeley results were announced by PERB; results for Santa Cruz, San Diego, Davis, Irvine, Riverside and Santa Barbara were due around June 17, 1999. Merced and San Francisco units were certified later (the 2026 agreement lists their separate PERB petitions).

summary: The first collective bargaining agreement between UC and the UAW for academic student employees took effect on June 1, 2000, after a long organizing campaign; it expired October 1, 2003.
UC recognized the UAW as the representative of Graduate Student Researchers in a Recognition Agreement dated December 8, 2021, after PERB certified the unit.
UC and UAW 4811 agreed to extend the 2022 BX and BR contracts to January 1, 2026, with a 4% increase on October 1, 2025, and to begin successor negotiations by July 7, 2025.
The extended 2022 BX and BR contracts expired on January 1, 2026, before a successor was reached.

UAW 4811 members passed an unfair-labor-practice strike authorization vote on February 13, 2026, with more than 93.3% of voters in favor. The union called off the strike when tentative agreements were reached in March.

After four weeks of confidential mediation, UC reached tentative agreements with UAW 4811 on Friday, March 13, 2026, for the unified ASE and GSR unit (and two staff units). The UC System Provost's letter of March 17, 2026 announced them to faculty.

UAW 4811 members ratified the agreement in a vote open from March 17 to March 20, 2026. In the ASE and GSR unit, 14,251 of 15,976 voters (89.2%) voted yes; across the three units voting together, 19,359 of 21,161 (91.5%).
Graduate employees at the University of Iowa organized the Campaign to Organize Graduate Students (COGS) in the spring of 1993.

In the fall of 1995 COGS members voted to affiliate with the United Electrical, Radio and Machine Workers of America (UE), after a first campaign affiliated with the Service Employees International Union (SEIU) lost its election in the spring of 1994.
note: The source does not give the vote's exact date or its count.

summary: In the spring of 1996 COGS won its representation election 949 to 667, making UE Local 896-COGS the bargaining agent for over 2,600 graduate employees; a first attempt, affiliated with SEIU in the spring of 1994, had fallen 70 votes short.
note: The source does not give the election's exact date.

summary: In the National Labor Relations Board election, 1,599 voted for representation by the Graduate Student Workers Organizing Committee-UAW and 122 against, of 2,861 eligible voters; the NLRB issued the tally on February 17, 2023.
note: The union filed its petition on December 14, 2022, and the NLRB issued the notice of election on February 1, 2023. The union and the UAW describe the result as 93% voting yes.

summary: The NLRB certified the Graduate Student Workers Organizing Committee-UAW as the representative of USC's graduate student workers on February 27, 2023; the 2023 agreement's recognition article rests on that certification.

Strike threat, not a strike. The bargaining team reached a tentative agreement with the university on November 26, 2023, one day before workers were set to strike, after nearly eight months of negotiations.
Over 80% of USC's graduate student workers voted to ratify their first contract; GSWOC-UAW announced the result on December 7, 2023, after three days of voting.
Underpaid@UT, a graduate student pay campaign organized since 2016, decided to unionize.
The Graduate Workers Union was founded, UT Austin's first grassroots labor union.
note: The article, published in November 2025, gives the day and month only; the year is 2025 from its description of the union as newly formed and advocating "for the past two months".

summary: Workers at the University of Utah and Utah State University announced United Campus Workers of Utah, CWA Local 7765, on February 26, 2024, naming teaching and research assistants among its members.
The Teaching Assistants' Association was formed in the spring of 1966 at an anti-draft sit-in on the Madison campus.

After the university agreed to abide by an election supervised by the Wisconsin Employment Relations Commission, teaching assistants chose the TAA as their exclusive bargaining agent in May 1969, with 77 percent of the vote; the first contract followed a strike in 1970.

After a 1985 state law gave teaching and project assistants bargaining rights, they chose the TAA as their bargaining agent in a representation election in the spring of 1987; the university had ended the earlier bargaining framework in 1980.

Graduate students at UW began organizing the union, then the Graduate Student Employee Action Coalition (GSEAC), in winter 1998; a year later its members voted to affiliate with the United Auto Workers.
After UW refused to bargain, saying state law prohibited it, the union struck for two weeks in June 2001, disrupting end-of-quarter grading.
note: By spring 2000 the union had collected signed authorization cards from 80 percent of the teaching assistants, readers and tutors.

summary: A state law (Chapter 34, Laws of 2002, RCW 41.56.203) extended collective bargaining rights to UW's academic student employees, taking effect when the Governor signed it on March 14, 2002; GSEAC/UAW then petitioned the Public Employment Relations Commission for certification.

In a mail-ballot representation election run by the Public Employment Relations Commission, 1,391 voted for GSEAC/UAW and 979 for no representation, of about 4,569 eligible; the tally issued March 18, 2004.
note: On April 6, 2004 the Commission denied the objections filed against the election and sent the case back for certification of the union.

summary: UAW Local 4121 members ratified their first collective bargaining agreement with UW in 2004.
note: The University's labor history page says the union negotiated its first contract later in 2002; the union's own history gives 2004 for ratification, after the 2004 certification election.

summary: UW and UAW Local 4121 reached a tentative agreement on the successor contract after mediated sessions with a Public Employment Relations Commission mediator.
Members ratified the 2024-2027 agreement; UW announced it on May 23, 2024, and the contract took effect May 19, 2024, the ratification date under Article 39.
In the fall of 2020, first-year graduate students across the College of Engineering began organizing what became the Virginia Tech Graduate Labor Union.
The Virginia Tech Graduate Labor Union announced itself publicly at a rally on September 5, 2023.
Graduate and professional workers voted to form a union in early 2023, with 91 percent of the vote.
Local 33 members ratified the first contract 1,705 to 10 in a vote held December 15 and 16, 2023; Article 38 makes it effective on ratification, December 16.
The union was founded in 1990 as the Graduate Employees and Students Organization (GESO), which took the name Local 33 in 2016.
note: The Yale Daily News traces GESO's roots to TA Solidarity, a graduate student group founded in 1987.

summary: The National Labor Relations Board certified UNITE HERE Local 33 as the representative of Yale's graduate and professional student workers on January 18, 2023, after a tally issued January 9 counted 1,860 votes for the union and 179 against.
note: Local 33 filed for the election in October 2022 and the voting was held in November and December 2022. The 2023 agreement's recognition clause refers to this certification.
